msrc19.title: Trends, Challenges, and Strategic Shifts in the Software Vulnerability Mitigation Landscape
msrc19.text: M. Miller (Microsoft Security Response Center). “Trends, Challenges, and Strategic Shifts in the Software Vulnerability Mitigation Landscape.” BlueHat IL, 2019. The source of the widely quoted figure that ~70% of the CVEs Microsoft assigns are memory-safety issues.

chromium.title: Memory safety (Chromium security documentation)
chromium.text: The Chromium Projects. “Memory safety.” Chromium security documentation, chromium.org. Reports that around 70% of Chromium's serious security bugs are memory-safety problems.

android22.title: Memory Safe Languages in Android 13
android22.text: J. Vander Stoep. “Memory Safe Languages in Android 13.” Google Security Blog, 2022. Reports memory-safety bugs falling as a share of Android's total vulnerabilities as new code moved to memory-safe languages.

checkedc18.title: Checked C: Making C Safe by Extension
checkedc18.text: A. S. Elliott, A. Ruef, M. Hicks, D. Tarditi. “Checked C: Making C Safe by Extension.” IEEE Cybersecurity Development (SecDev) 2018.

cheri15.title: CHERI: A Hybrid Capability-System Architecture for Scalable Software Compartmentalization
cheri15.text: R. N. M. Watson, J. Woodruff, P. G. Neumann, S. W. Moore, J. Anderson, D. Chisnall, N. Dave, B. Davis, K. Gudka, B. Laurie, S. J. Murdoch, R. Norton, M. Roe, S. Son, M. Vadera. “CHERI: A Hybrid Capability-System Architecture for Scalable Software Compartmentalization.” IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2015.

softbound09.title: SoftBound: Highly Compatible and Complete Spatial Memory Safety for C
softbound09.text: S. Nagarakatte, J. Zhao, M. M. K. Martin, S. Zdancewic. “SoftBound: Highly Compatible and Complete Spatial Memory Safety for C.” PLDI 2009.

cets10.title: CETS: Compiler-Enforced Temporal Safety for C
cets10.text: S. Nagarakatte, J. Zhao, M. M. K. Martin, S. Zdancewic. “CETS: Compiler-Enforced Temporal Safety for C.” ISMM 2010.

asan12.title: AddressSanitizer: A Fast Address Sanity Checker
asan12.text: K. Serebryany, D. Bruening, A. Potapenko, D. Vyukov. “AddressSanitizer: A Fast Address Sanity Checker.” USENIX ATC 2012.

valgrind07.title: Valgrind: A Framework for Heavyweight Dynamic Binary Instrumentation
valgrind07.text: N. Nethercote, J. Seward. “Valgrind: A Framework for Heavyweight Dynamic Binary Instrumentation.” PLDI 2007. Callgrind, the instruction counter behind every cost figure here, is one of its tools.

astrauskas20.title: How Do Programmers Use Unsafe Rust?
astrauskas20.text: V. Astrauskas, C. Matheja, F. Poli, P. Müller, A. J. Summers. “How Do Programmers Use Unsafe Rust?” OOPSLA 2020 (PACMPL vol. 4).

evans20.title: Is Rust Used Safely by Software Developers?
evans20.text: A. N. Evans, B. Campbell, M. L. Soffa. “Is Rust Used Safely by Software Developers?” ICSE 2020.

qin20.title: Understanding Memory and Thread Safety Practices and Issues in Real-World Rust Programs
qin20.text: B. Qin, Y. Chen, Z. Yu, L. Song, Y. Zhang. “Understanding Memory and Thread Safety Practices and Issues in Real-World Rust Programs.” PLDI 2020.

rustbelt18.title: RustBelt: Securing the Foundations of the Rust Programming Language
rustbelt18.text: R. Jung, J.-H. Jourdan, R. Krebbers, D. Dreyer. “RustBelt: Securing the Foundations of the Rust Programming Language.” POPL 2018 (PACMPL vol. 2).

stackedborrows20.title: Stacked Borrows: An Aliasing Model for Rust
stackedborrows20.text: R. Jung, H.-H. Dang, J. Kang, D. Dreyer. “Stacked Borrows: An Aliasing Model for Rust.” POPL 2020 (PACMPL vol. 4). The aliasing discipline Miri checks by default.

c2rust.title: C2Rust
c2rust.text: Immunant, Inc. “C2Rust: migrate C code to Rust.” https://github.com/immunant/c2rust. A transpiler producing unsafe Rust from C.

laertes21.title: Translating C to Safer Rust
laertes21.text: M. Emre, R. Schroeder, K. Dewey, B. Hardekopf. “Translating C to Safer Rust.” OOPSLA 2021 (PACMPL vol. 5).

userstudy25.title: Translating C To Rust: Lessons from a User Study
userstudy25.text: R. Li, B. Wang, T. Li, P. Saxena, A. Kundu. “Translating C To Rust: Lessons from a User Study.” Network and Distributed System Security (NDSS) Symposium 2025. 33 participants produced 31 pure-safe-Rust translations of 8 C programs of 322–536 lines.

verus23.title: Verus: Verifying Rust Programs using Linear Ghost Types
verus23.text: A. Lattuada, T. Hance, C. Cho, M. Brun, I. Subasinghe, Y. Zhou, J. Howell, B. Parno, C. Hawblitzel. “Verus: Verifying Rust Programs using Linear Ghost Types.” OOPSLA 2023.

z3.title: Z3: An Efficient SMT Solver
z3.text: L. de Moura, N. Bjørner. “Z3: An Efficient SMT Solver.” TACAS 2008. The solver behind every proof result reported here.

prusti19.title: Leveraging Rust Types for Modular Specification and Verification
prusti19.text: V. Astrauskas, P. Müller, F. Poli, A. J. Summers. “Leveraging Rust Types for Modular Specification and Verification.” OOPSLA 2019 (PACMPL vol. 3).

creusot22.title: Creusot: A Foundry for the Deductive Verification of Rust Programs
creusot22.text: X. Denis, J.-H. Jourdan, C. Marché. “Creusot: A Foundry for the Deductive Verification of Rust Programs.” ICFEM 2022.

kani22.title: Verifying Dynamic Trait Objects in Rust
kani22.text: A. VanHattum, D. Schwartz-Narbonne, N. Chong, A. Sampson. “Verifying Dynamic Trait Objects in Rust.” ICSE-SEIP 2022. The Kani model checker for Rust.

ctverif16.title: Verifying Constant-Time Implementations
ctverif16.text: J. B. Almeida, M. Barbosa, G. Barthe, F. Dupressoir, M. Emmi. “Verifying Constant-Time Implementations.” USENIX Security 2016. Reduces constant-time, a relational property, to a safety property of a product program.

jasmin17.title: Jasmin: High-Assurance and High-Speed Cryptography
jasmin17.text: J. B. Almeida, M. Barbosa, G. Barthe, A. Blot, B. Grégoire, V. Laporte, T. Oliveira, et al. “Jasmin: High-Assurance and High-Speed Cryptography.” ACM CCS 2017.

fact19.title: FaCT: A DSL for Timing-Sensitive Computation
fact19.text: S. Cauligi, G. Soeller, B. Johannesmeyer, F. Brown, R. S. Wahby, J. Renner, B. Grégoire, G. Barthe, R. Jhala, D. Stefan. “FaCT: A DSL for Timing-Sensitive Computation.” PLDI 2019.

compcertct.title: Formal Verification of a Constant-Time Preserving C Compiler
compcertct.text: G. Barthe, S. Blazy, B. Grégoire, R. Hutin, V. Laporte, D. Pichardie, A. Trieu. “Formal Verification of a Constant-Time Preserving C Compiler.” POPL 2020 (PACMPL vol. 4).

mytkowicz09.title: Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!
mytkowicz09.text: T. Mytkowicz, A. Diwan, M. Hauswirth, P. F. Sweeney. “Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!” ASPLOS 2009. Measurement bias from environment size and link order, large enough to invert conclusions.

stabilizer13.title: STABILIZER: Statistically Sound Performance Evaluation
stabilizer13.text: C. Curtsinger, E. D. Berger. “STABILIZER: Statistically Sound Performance Evaluation.” ASPLOS 2013. Repeatedly re-randomises code and data layout so layout effects can be treated statistically.
